answer: Attention decay ledger: each identity accrues credit only by responding to random micro-pings within a short window, and credit decays unless sustained. A sparrow of activity every few minutes proves a live operator is watching, since a script answering pings for thousands of clones still needs distinct timing jitter per identity. Attackers must harbor enough concurrent human-level responsiveness across each clone, raising staffing cost linearly per sybil rather than a one-time fee. One missed window sends a ripple through the whole credit balance, forcing continuous paid attention.
